gas-gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.title: Gastroesophageal reflux disease
gas-gastroesophageal-reflux-disease.summary: Retrosternal burning after meals that worsens when lying flat with an unremarkable abdominal examination with a normal weight trend is the presentation that defines gastroesophageal reflux disease. An empiric trial of acid suppression without initial testing confirms it, and once-daily proton pump inhibitor therapy with lifestyle modification is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Gastroesophageal reflux disease describes the clinical picture of retrosternal burning after meals that worsens when lying flat produced by transient lower esophageal sphincter relaxation permitting acid reflux. This entry is arranged in the order the problem tends to be encountered: what drives it, how it appears, how it is confirmed, and what is done first.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that alarm features — dysphagia, weight loss, bleeding — are what convert empiric therapy into endoscopy.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is transient lower esophageal sphincter relaxation permitting acid reflux. Its consequences account for both the symptoms the patient reports and the signs found on examination.

Reserve within the affected system means measurable derangement often precedes anything the patient notices. Understanding this is what makes once-daily proton pump inhibitor therapy with lifestyle modification the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Retrosternal burning after meals that worsens when lying flat is the complaint that brings the patient in, and its evolution over days to weeks is the detail worth pinning down.

Presentations at the extremes of age are frequently less typical, and a normal early course does not exclude the diagnosis. A history of retrosternal burning after meals that worsens when lying flat in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: An unremarkable abdominal examination with a normal weight trend is the examination finding that most reliably separates this from its closest mimics.
A normal examination early in the course is common and does not argue meaningfully against the diagnosis.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: Evaluation begins with an empiric trial of acid suppression without initial testing, which answers the question directly rather than narrowing it by degrees.

Testing before the pre-test probability has been thought through produces results that are difficult to act on in either direction. The alternative most often confused with it is cirrhosis with portal hypertension, which is compared below.

gas-clostridioides-difficile-colitis.title: Clostridioides difficile colitis
gas-clostridioides-difficile-colitis.summary: Profuse watery diarrhea beginning days after a course of antibiotics with lower abdominal tenderness with low-grade fever is the presentation that defines clostridioides difficile colitis. Stool testing for the organism and its toxin confirms it, and oral standard-of-care antibiotic therapy with cessation of the inciting agent is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: The presentation that names clostridioides difficile colitis is profuse watery diarrhea beginning days after a course of antibiotics; the process behind it is toxin-mediated colonic mucosal injury after antibiotic disruption of the flora. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. paras: What drives the picture is toxin-mediated colonic mucosal injury after antibiotic disruption of the flora. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes oral standard-of-care antibiotic therapy with cessation of the inciting agent the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

paras: The history classically centres on profuse watery diarrhea beginning days after a course of antibiotics; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

gas-irritable-bowel-syndrome.title: Irritable bowel syndrome

paras: Irritable bowel syndrome describes the clinical picture of six months of crampy abdominal pain relieved by defecation, with variable stool form produced by disordered gut-brain interaction with visceral hypersensitivity. The account that follows moves from the underlying process to the bedside picture, then to confirmation and initial treatment — the order in which the problem is usually met.

The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that a confident positive diagnosis prevents the escalating-workup spiral.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: The process at work is disordered gut-brain interaction with visceral hypersensitivity. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

The rate at which the process develops matters as much as its extent: a gradual change is tolerated where an abrupt one of the same size is not. Understanding this is what makes dietary modification with symptom-directed therapy and reassurance the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

paras: The history classically centres on six months of crampy abdominal pain relieved by defecation, with variable stool form; what refines it is the time course rather than the severity at any one moment.

gas-upper-gastrointestinal-bleeding.title: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
gas-upper-gastrointestinal-bleeding.summary: Two episodes of coffee-ground emesis with black tarry stools with resting tachycardia with melena on rectal examination is the presentation that defines upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Hemodynamic assessment with early risk stratification confirms it, and volume resuscitation, acid suppression, and endoscopy after stabilization is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding is defined by two episodes of coffee-ground emesis with black tarry stools, arising from mucosal vessel erosion within the proximal digestive tract. This entry is arranged in the order the problem tends to be encountered: what drives it, how it appears, how it is confirmed, and what is done first.

How often the problem is seen depends on where the counting is done, and case definitions have shifted enough over time that historical series need reading with care. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that resuscitation precedes endoscopy — the scope confirms what stabilization made safe.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: At the centre of the problem is mucosal vessel erosion within the proximal digestive tract. Tracing the picture back to that single process explains why the individual findings travel together rather than appearing in isolation.

Compensatory responses mask the process early and fail late, which is why the interval between the first abnormality and the first symptom can be long. Understanding this is what makes volume resuscitation, acid suppression, and endoscopy after stabilization the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: Patients most often describe two episodes of coffee-ground emesis with black tarry stools, and it is the tempo of that history — how quickly it arrived and whether it is progressing — that carries the diagnostic weight.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of two episodes of coffee-ground emesis with black tarry stools in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.

sections.heading: Examination
paras: Resting tachycardia with melena on rectal examination is the examination finding that most reliably separates this from its closest mimics.
Interobserver agreement for the classic signs is only moderate, which is a reason to weigh them alongside the history rather than above it.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
paras: The first investigation is hemodynamic assessment with early risk stratification; ordering it early avoids a sequence of tests that each exclude one possibility.

Incidental findings are common enough that the question being asked should be settled before the study is requested. The alternative most often confused with it is clostridioides difficile colitis, which is compared below.

gas-chronic-hepatitis.title: Chronic hepatitis
gas-chronic-hepatitis.summary: An incidental finding of elevated aminotransferases on routine testing with a soft, nontender abdomen with no stigmata of chronic disease is the presentation that defines chronic hepatitis. Viral serologies with metabolic and autoimmune screening confirms it, and therapy directed at the specific underlying cause is the initial management.

sections.heading: Overview
paras: Chronic hepatitis is defined by an incidental finding of elevated aminotransferases on routine testing, arising from ongoing hepatocellular inflammation from a persistent inciting process. Sections below follow one conventional sequence — mechanism, presentation, confirmation, management — and each can be read on its own.

Reported frequency varies with the population studied and with the threshold chosen to define a case, so figures quoted in different sources are rarely directly comparable. The teaching point most often attached to this topic is that a patterned panel beats serial re-checking of the same abnormal enzymes.

sections.heading: Mechanism
paras: At the centre of the problem is ongoing hepatocellular inflammation from a persistent inciting process. Once that is established, the downstream findings follow in a predictable order, which is what makes the presentation recognisable at the bedside.

The rate at which the process develops matters as much as its extent: a gradual change is tolerated where an abrupt one of the same size is not. Understanding this is what makes therapy directed at the specific underlying cause the rational first response rather than an arbitrary one.

sections.heading: Clinical presentation
paras: An incidental finding of elevated aminotransferases on routine testing is the complaint that brings the patient in, and its evolution over days to weeks is the detail worth pinning down.

Comorbid disease alters the picture, sometimes to the point that the usual pattern is unrecognisable. A history of an incidental finding of elevated aminotransferases on routine testing in the right context is enough to bring the diagnosis to the front of the differential.
